Equation

Source: R/ooxml_run_equation.R
run_equation.Rd

Create an equation written in LaTeX, to be used in a paragraph made with fpar().

The equation is converted by the package 'equatags' into an 'Office' equation ('Office Open XML Math'): it stays editable in 'Word' and 'PowerPoint'. Use it with body_add_fpar() in a 'Word' document, with ph_with() in a 'PowerPoint' presentation and with sheet_add_drawing() in an 'Excel' workbook, where equations are in a text box ('Excel' does not accept equations in cells).

In HTML (to_html()), equations are drawn by 'KaTeX' (its stylesheet is linked). In RTF documents (rtf_add()), they are images drawn by 'equatags' (R >= 4.3), placed on the baseline of the text; with an older version of R, the LaTeX source is written as text, with a warning.

Usage

run_equation(x, prop = NULL)

Arguments

x

the equation, a LaTeX string. The functions supported by 'KaTeX' can be used, see https://katex.org/docs/supported.html.

prop

formatting text properties returned by fp_text() or fp_text_lite(). Only the font size and the color are used, the font is the math font of the document ('Cambria Math' by default). With NULL, the default size and color of the document or of the shape.

Inline and display style

As in 'Word', the style of the equation depends on its paragraph:

  • an equation alone in its paragraph uses the display style (larger fractions, limits above and below sums) and is aligned with the alignment of the paragraph (argument text.align of fp_par());

  • an equation in a paragraph that contains something else, even a space, uses the inline style.

usage

You can use this function in conjunction with fpar to create paragraphs consisting of differently formatted text parts. You can also use this function as an r chunk in an R Markdown document made with package officedown.

See also

Other run functions for reporting: external_img(), floating_external_img(), ftext(), hyperlink_ftext(), run_autonum(), run_bookmark(), run_columnbreak(), run_comment(), run_footnote(), run_footnoteref(), run_linebreak(), run_pagebreak(), run_reference(), run_tab(), run_word_field(), run_wordtext()

Examples

library(officer)

quadratic <- "x = \\frac{-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}"
euler <- "e^{i\\pi} + 1 = 0"

doc <- read_docx()
# an equation alone in its paragraph: display style, centered
doc <- body_add_fpar(
  doc,
  fpar(run_equation(quadratic), fp_p = fp_par(text.align = "center"))
)
# an equation in a sentence: inline style, 14 points, in red
doc <- body_add_fpar(
  doc,
  fpar(
    "Euler's identity: ",
    run_equation(euler, prop = fp_text_lite(font.size = 14, color = "red")),
    "."
  )
)
print(doc, target = tempfile(fileext = ".docx"))

pres <- read_pptx()
pres <- add_slide(pres, layout = "Title and Content")
pres <- ph_with(
  pres,
  block_list(
    fpar("The quadratic formula:"),
    fpar(run_equation(quadratic), fp_p = fp_par(text.align = "center"))
  ),
  location = ph_location_type("body")
)
print(pres, target = tempfile(fileext = ".pptx"))

wb <- read_xlsx()
wb <- sheet_add_drawing(
  wb,
  value = fpar(run_equation(quadratic)),
  sheet = "Feuil1",
  anchor = "C2"
)
print(wb, target = tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx"))
